figures_added.what: Reflection-in-the-x-axis scene for the duck box: a horizontal water line (the mirror), the duck marked 5 cm above, and its reflection the same 5 cm below marked '?'. The unknown height (box answer -5) is left as '?', so the figure makes the reflection concrete without revealing the value. Theme-safe: currentColor line/labels/'?', soft #60a5fa water fill at 0.18 opacity, amber duck dot.

The given base curve y = x^2 (points x=-3..3 verified to satisfy y=x^2) with its vertex (0,0) highlighted in amber. The question transforms this to y = (x+1)^2 - 4 and asks for the new vertex y (-4); the transformed parabola is NOT drawn, so the answer stays hidden while the student sees the vertex being moved.

The given curve y = sin x over 0 to 360 degrees (points every 15 degrees verified against sin). This is exactly the figure an exam prints before asking for the equation of its reflection in the x-axis. The answer is a multiple-choice equation, not shown on the graph.

The given base curve y = x^2 with vertex (0,0) highlighted. The problem translates it to y = (x-3)^2 + 1 and asks for the x-component of the translation vector (3). Only the base curve is drawn, so the horizontal shift (the answer) is not visible on the figure.

notes: Diagram pass only. Added three Chart.js base-curve figures and one opener SVG; no question text, solutions, guided_steps, hints, or misconceptions were touched (verified: object is byte-identical to the fetched live row once the four additions are removed). Figures were limited to the three problems that name a concrete printable curve (y=x^2 twice, y=sin x once), which is what an exam paper actually prints; every one shows the GIVEN base curve only so no answer is revealed. All chart points were recomputed against their equations. The remaining bank problems are abstract y=f(x) with coordinates supplied in the text, or read a transformation straight off a function-notation equation (direction/axis multiple choice), so an exam gives no figure and forcing a grid would be the decoration the spec warns against. Opener SVG is self-contained (~1.1KB, viewBox + role=img + aria-label, currentColor strokes/text, soft translucent water fill, no external refs).
